Dornell Textiles to Reopen Former Mill

(Ashford, May 19)—Dornell Textiles announced on Monday that it will begin producing outdoor fabrics
at the former Kemp Mill on River Road this autumn. The building, which has been empty since 2019, is
being repaired and fitted with modern weaving equipment. [1]

The company, which currently operates one plant in Greenvale, makes water-resistant fabric used in
tents, backpacks, and boat covers. [2] Demand for these products has risen sharply over the past
three years, and the Greenvale plant has been running at full capacity since last spring.

Dornell expects to hire about 150 workers for the Ashford site. [3] Applicants with no experience
will be considered, as the company will provide eight weeks of paid training. Hiring events will be
held at the Ashford Public Library on June 7 and June 14.

Mayor Diane Coyle welcomed the news. "Kemp Mill was once the town's largest employer," she said.
"It's wonderful to see the lights back on." [4]
sets.tr:
도넬 텍스타일, 옛 방직 공장 재가동

(애슈퍼드, 5월 19일)—도넬 텍스타일은 월요일, 올가을부터 리버 로드의 옛 켐프 방직 공장에서 아웃도어 원단 생산을 시작한다고 발표했다. 2019년부터 비어 있던 이 건물은 현재 수리 중이며 최신 직조 설비가 설치되고 있다. [1]

Farmers' Cooperative Opens Shared Processing Center

(Millford, August 8)—Small farms in Brayton County now have a place to wash, sort, and package their
produce without buying expensive equipment of their own. The Brayton Growers Cooperative opened its
new processing center on Lowell Road last week. [1]

The 2,000-square-meter facility was paid for in part by a state agricultural grant. Member farms can
rent time on the center's machines by the hour and store their produce in its cold rooms for up to
ten days. [2]

"Before, many of our members could sell only at farmers' markets," said cooperative president Ruth
Abara. "Grocery chains want produce that is packed and labeled to a certain standard. Now our
members can meet those requirements." [3] Two regional supermarket chains have already agreed to
carry produce packed at the center.

The cooperative currently has 46 member farms. Membership costs $300 a year, and the cooperative
hopes to attract at least 20 new members by next spring. [4] Information sessions for interested
growers will be held on the first Tuesday of every month.
